name: Alamos Gold Inc.

profile.description: Alamos Gold is a Canadian intermediate gold producer operating the Island Gold District (Island Gold and Magino, combined through the 2024 Argonaut Gold acquisition) and the Young-Davidson underground mine in Ontario, plus the Mulatos District in Sonora, Mexico. Its development pipeline includes the Island Gold Phase 3+ expansion and the Lynn Lake project in Manitoba. Co-founder John McCluskey has led the company as CEO since 2003. 2026 production guidance is 510,000-560,000 ounces, lowered after a seismic event at Young-Davidson.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Alamos turned Island Gold into one of the world's highest-grade underground gold mines, an achievement recognized with McCluskey's 2023 PDAC Viola R. MacMillan Award. It brought La Yaqui Grande into production and combined Island Gold with the adjacent Magino mill through the 2024 Argonaut acquisition, reshaping its growth profile [4][5]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI deployment or quantified AI savings is disclosed. Management references upgraded information and operational systems only [5]. Market Share (1/2): Alamos is a meaningful mid-tier producer (about 0.5M oz per year) but not a category leader. Pipeline (2/2): The Island Gold Phase 3+ shaft expansion and the Lynn Lake project have defined timelines and are targeted to lift production toward about 900K-1M oz by 2030 [1][2]. R&D (0/1): There is no material R&D spending, as is typical for miners.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Alamos describes its aim as building a sustainable, Canada-focused gold producer that creates value for all stakeholders, which is clear but standard for a miner [6]. Community Impact (1/2): The company reported $1.5M of community investment and charitable giving in 2024, along with Indigenous partnership agreements around Island Gold and Lynn Lake. This is general and modest relative to about $1.8B of revenue [6]. Employee Retention (1/2): Co-founder McCluskey has served as CEO since 2003, and the May 2026 promotions of two internal VPs suggest bench development, but no turnover data is disclosed [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): The CEO holds about 0.2%, and no meaningful net insider buying was identified [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored at 10.0/10. Every metric meets its target [3]. D/E of 4.6% scores 1.0. ROE of 23.6% scores 1.0 at 2x weight. YoY revenue growth of 10.4% (Q3 2026 revenue of $510.4M, +10%, on a $4,258/oz realized gold price) scores 1.0 [1]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 19.3% ($748M in 2020 to $1.81B in 2025) scores 1.0 at 2x weight. Forward P/E of 9.95 scores 1.0. Profit margin of 46.7% scores 1.0. Forward PEG of about 0.66 (forward P/E of 9.95 divided by roughly 15% implied forward EPS growth from the trailing-to-forward P/E spread) scores 1.0 at 2x weight. Even with PEG excluded, the score would still be 10. Liquidity is about $113M per day, well above the floor.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Gold mining means physically extracting ore from underground and open-pit deposits in Ontario and Sonora, and AI cannot substitute for the product or the process [1]. Gold's role as a monetary and safe-haven asset is unaffected by AI, and AI-driven demand for electronics adds marginally to industrial use. Exploration targeting and mine automation are enablers for the industry, not threats. AI Opportunity (0/1): Alamos earns no AI-related revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Alamos has unusual continuity for a miner: the same co-founder CEO for 23 years and a long, patient build-out of Island Gold that Sinek would respect. Its purpose, however, is still framed as value creation rather than a Just Cause, and its strategic shifts have been portfolio moves rather than a reinvention driven by purpose [4][5].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company's purpose centers on being a responsible, low-cost, growing gold producer that creates value for stakeholders [6]. That is a business objective rather than a vision of a better future, and it reads much like any peer's.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is exceptional, with McCluskey as CEO since co-founding in 2003. The May 2026 internal promotions and McCluskey's emphasis on 'depth of the management team' indicate a stable organization [5]. No employee-sentiment data is available to show more than adequate trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Alamos frames its position in terms of grade, AISC and per-share growth versus mid-tier peers. There is no evidence of competitors being treated as teachers.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Over the last decade Alamos shifted from a Mexico- and Turkey-centered portfolio to a Canada-focused one. It exited the Turkish projects after licensing disputes and an investment-treaty claim, and added Island Gold, Magino and Lynn Lake [4][7]. This is substantial portfolio adaptation within the same gold-mining model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): McCluskey won the 2023 PDAC Viola R. MacMillan Award specifically for 'a willingness to take risks' in acquiring and developing Island Gold [5]. The company has committed to the multi-year Phase 3+ shaft expansion and the Lynn Lake build despite AISC rising to $1,956/oz and guidance being cut after the Young-Davidson seismic event, consistently choosing long-life capacity over near-term free cash flow [1][2].

investment_thesis: Alamos combines a fortress balance sheet (D/E of 4.6%) with strong profitability (46.7% net margin, 23.6% ROE) and one of the clearest organic growth profiles among mid-tier producers [3]. Q3 2026 revenue rose 10% to $510.4M at a realized gold price of $4,258/oz (+27%), and earnings from operations were $268.7M [1]. The Island Gold Phase 3+ expansion and Lynn Lake are targeted to lift output toward about 900K-1M oz by 2030 from a Canadian, low-jurisdiction-risk base, and the stock trades at a forward P/E of about 10 after falling from a 50-day average of $34 [1][3].
thesis_continued: Operations have weakened. Q3 2026 ounces sold fell to 118,361, AISC rose to $1,956/oz on inflation and lower Island Gold grades, and full-year guidance was cut to 510-560K oz after a seismic event at Young-Davidson [1]. Earnings are highly leveraged to the gold price, so a retreat from record levels near $4,000+/oz would compress margins quickly, and large expansion projects carry cost-overrun and schedule risk. The dividend yields only about 0.55%, and the Inspire Impact score is a neutral 0.
key_catalysts: Island Gold Phase 3+ shaft commissioning and ramp-up of the combined Island Gold-Magino operation, lifting production and lowering AISC [2]
Lynn Lake construction progress toward first gold, adding a third Canadian growth asset [2]
Recovery of Young-Davidson production after the seismic event, restoring output toward pre-event guidance [1]
key_risks: Operational: AISC rising to $1,956/oz in Q3 2026 and lower Island Gold grades, plus seismic risk at deep underground mines like Young-Davidson [1]
Gold price exposure: earnings and the 46.7% margin depend on gold above $4,000/oz [3]
Execution risk on simultaneous large capital projects (Phase 3+, Lynn Lake) during cost inflation
